recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for FHIR-46399. Treat FHIR-51073 and FHIR-49977 as separate follow-up issues if further reconciliation is needed, because they concern existing binding instances and tooling extension packaging rather than the core key mechanism.
issue_request: FHIR-46399 was Applied/Persuasive for R6 and requested a way to distinguish constraining an existing additionalBinding from introducing a new additionalBinding. The accepted resolution added a 0..1 id key to additional bindings, a best-practice key.exists() invariant, and profiling guidance that derived profiles constrain base additional bindings by using the same key.
initial_application: Commit 757595c1e9a3b3e452fb3651f4d3eaabf32a9c60 explicitly applied FHIR-46399 by adding ElementDefinition.binding.additional.key to source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml, adding the best-practice invariant on ElementDefinition.binding.additional, and inserting the requested same-key derivation rule in source/profiling.html.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively includes the elementdefinition page and declares ElementDefinition normative, so the inspected files are in current build scope. The originating Zulip thread confirms that the key was requested to let downstream profiles identify constrained additional bindings. Confluence references only schedule or relate FHIR-46399 with FHIR-46350 and do not alter the Jira decision. Later related issues FHIR-51073 and FHIR-49977 concern follow-up key population and FHIR-tools extension packaging rather than the core mechanism itself.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the active source already contains the requested structural key, best-practice invariant, and profiling prose. The published commit is an empty audit record documenting that no duplicate or redundant edit is needed.
